TYPE workout

TYPE nutrition
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary nutrition:
    name "Body recomposition: optimize body fat, support training recovery, avoid shoulder strain; dairy-free? (not specified) maintain pain-free ROM"

PHASES
  PHASE "Phase A" (12 weeks):
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Daily plan "Macronutrient targets and timing":
        macronutrients:
          calories: "estimate at maintenance plus small deficit if fat loss desired; tailor to client weight; start with 0% deficit"
          protein: "1.6..2.2 g per kg bodyweight" 
          carbs: "rest of calories after protein and fat are set"
          fat: "0.8..1.0 g per kg bodyweight"
        meals:
          meal_1: "protein source, complex carb, fats"
          meal_2: "protein, carbs, fats"
          meal_3: "protein, carbs, fats"
          meal_4: "protein, fiber-rich vegetables, fats"
        hydration:
          water_intake: "30..40 ml per kg bodyweight"
        timing:
          pre_workout: "protein + carb, 30–90 minutes pre-session"
          post_workout: "protein + carb within 60–120 minutes post-session"
        supplements (optional and per clinician):
          creatine: "3–5 g daily"
          vitamin_d3: "as per bloodwork"
          omega_3: "1–2 g EPA+DHA daily"
        restrictions:
          no foodName restrictions provided
    WEEK 4:
      DAY Daily plan "Progress check and tweaks":
        notes:
          - adjust calories to target weight change
          - ensure protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg
          - prioritize protein intake around training
          - align carbohydrate timing with training days
    WEEK 8:
      DAY Daily plan "Fat-loss or maintenance recalibration":
        notes:
          - if fat loss pursued, slight deficit ( -250 to -500 kcal )
          - maintain protein target
          - ensure energy for workouts; adjust carbs around sessions
    WEEK 12:
      DAY Daily plan "Stability and maintenance":
        notes:
          - set long-term plan and handover to athlete lifestyle

NUTRITIONAL GUIDELINES
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight per day; distribute evenly across 3–5 meals.
- Carbohydrates: adjustable; provide enough to support training intensity and recovery; higher on training days, lower on rest days if fat loss target is pursued.
- Fats: 0.8–1.0 g/kg bodyweight per day; prioritize polyunsaturated and monounsaturated sources.
- Calorie target: start at maintenance or slight deficit if fat loss desired; reassess every 2–4 weeks.
- Hydration: baseline 30–40 ml/kg/day; adjust for sweat rate and climate.
- Timing: protein and carbs around training; include a protein-containing snack or meal within 1–2 hours post-workout.
- Fiber: aim for 25–35 g/day from vegetables, fruits, legumes, whole grains.
- Sleep: target 7–9 hours per night to support recovery.

DIETARY PRACTICES
- Emphasize whole foods: lean proteins, vegetables, fruits, whole grains, legumes, healthy fats.
- Limit highly processed foods and added sugars where possible.
- No overhead loading concerns in nutrition; no exercise restrictions.

MONITORING & ADJUSTMENTS
- Track bodyweight weekly; maintain or adjust based on goals.
- Monitor energy, sleep, mood, training performance; adjust intake if fatigue accumulates.
- Reassess every 2–4 weeks; adjust macros to keep progress aligned with goals.
- If symptoms of shoulder pain increase, ensure nutrition supports tissue repair (adequate protein, micronutrients like zinc, vitamin C, vitamin D if deficient).

Implement this nutrition plan in parallel with the 12-week training plan, ensuring protein targets are met, calories aligned with body composition goals, and meal timing supports training sessions.

NUTRITIONAL GUIDELINES
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight per day; distribute evenly across 3–5 meals.

- Fats: 0.8–1.0 g/kg bodyweight per day; prioritize polyunsaturated and monounsaturated sources.
- Calorie target: start at maintenance or slight deficit if fat loss desired; reassess every 2–4 weeks.
- Hydration: baseline 30–40 ml/kg/day; adjust for sweat rate and climate.
- Timing: protein and carbs around training; include a protein-containing snack or meal within 1–2 hours post-workout.
- Fiber: aim for 25–35 g/day from vegetables, fruits, legumes, whole grains.
- Sleep: target 7–9 hours per night to support recovery.

- Emphasize whole foods: lean proteins, vegetables, fruits, whole grains, legumes, healthy fats.
- Limit highly processed foods and added sugars where possible.

- Monitor energy, sleep, mood, training performance; adjust intake if fatigue accumulates.

- If symptoms of shoulder pain increase, ensure nutrition supports tissue repair (adequate protein, micronutrients like zinc, vitamin C, vitamin D if deficient).

- Cardio sessions are kept moderate to support climbing endurance without compromising recovery.
